first_frame: Cinematic 16:9 military-documentary film still, the opening frame of a documentary. Flat grey Sea of Japan water under heavy low cloud: a small converted American intelligence ship - a short, stubby grey ex-cargo hull with rust streaks, a single funnel, two tall antenna masts crowded with wire aerials and direction-finding loops - sits low in the water on the left, seen side-on from wave height. On the right, a fast grey subchaser closes on her beam, still at a distance. A few tiny silhouetted figures on deck, faces never visible. No hull numbers, no names, no readable flags. Photorealistic simulated-footage military-documentary recreation, never cartoon. Overcast maritime palette: flat slate-grey sky, iron-grey sea, rust-streaked deck steel, salt spray. Deep focus, natural documentary contrast, subtle film grain, restrained cinematic grade, crushed blacks. ONE SINGLE FULL-FRAME 16:9 PHOTOGRAPH - not a grid, collage, contact sheet or split-screen. The photograph fills the entire 16:9 frame edge to edge with NO black bars, NO letterboxing, NO pillarboxing, no border and no matte of any kind. No inset picture, no picture-in-picture panel, no camera HUD, no REC indicator, no timestamp. No text, letters, words, subtitles or captions anywhere in frame.
